title: An E exchange has a constructible integral model
statement: Use the coefficient construction [def-weil-pbc-continuous-integral-coefficients]. Fix prime ℓ, finite normed E/ℚ_ℓ, and a Cartesian square of separated finite-type schemes over a field k of positive prime characteristic different from ℓ, with proper f:X→Y and all maps over k. For every bounded constructible complex K of continuous E coefficient internal modules on X there is a bounded constructible integral complex M on X such that the image under integralScalarExtension on Y′ of its specified integral base-change component is isomorphic, as an arrow of the full E derived category on Y′, to the specified continuous E base-change component at K. No invertibility of either exchange component is asserted.

source.place: Lemma 6.8.13 and Proposition 6.8.14(2), integral lattices and rationalization; exchange compatibility in the condensed realization argument

proof.text: Identify the raw continuous E internal-module constructible category with the rationalized integral category by finite presentations on strata and the continuous coefficient realization. Lemma 6.8.13 supplies constructible integral lattices; do not assume that they are globally lisse. Refine the stratification, extend across its open and closed pieces, and clear finitely many denominators to lift the extension classes in bounded truncation triangles. This constructs an integral bounded constructible M and an isomorphism of its E scalar extension with K.

Use the proved continuousIntegralFunctions_isLocalization on compact profinite tests, and exact inverse image from the point, to identify coefficient scalar extension with inversion of ℓ. Identify E scalar extension with inversion of ℓ on these complexes. Exact localization commutes with pullback. Proper direct image is qcqs; continuity for uniformly bounded-below diagrams makes its comparison with the localization telescope invertible. Use bounded representatives and the common lower bound to apply continuity, rather than assuming arbitrary unbounded coproduct continuity.

The coefficient pullback and pushforward comparisons arise from the actual adjunction maps. Their unit and counit identities and coherent pullback composition identify the two unit-square-counit exchange formulas. The endpoint isomorphisms conjugate the integral arrow after E scalar extension to the continuous E arrow on the realization of M. Naturality along that realization isomorphism to K gives the stated Arrow isomorphism.

theorem continuousExchange_integral_model [IsProper f]
    (sq : IsPullback g' f' f g)
    (K : ProEtale.BoundedConstructible
      (condensedRingObj (Profinite.continuousMapRingObj E) X)) :
    ∃ M : ProEtale.BoundedConstructible (condensedRingObj (integralCoeff ℓ E) X),
      Nonempty (Arrow.mk ((integralScalarExtension ℓ E Y').map
          ((boundedConstructibleBaseChange (integralCoeff ℓ E) ℓ k sq.toCommSq).app M).hom) ≅
        Arrow.mk ((boundedConstructibleBaseChange (Profinite.continuousMapRingObj E) ℓ k
          sq.toCommSq).app K).hom)
